summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, alcohol abuse, and depression was admitted after being found obtunded at home by her daughter. She had stopped drinking alcohol cold turkey and discontinued her insulin due to nausea and abdominal pain, leading to diabetic ketoacidosis. On admission, she was hypothermic, had altered mental status, and lab findings showed severe metabolic acidosis, hyperkalemia, acute kidney injury, and anemia. She was treated with IV fluids, insulin infusion, and electrolyte correction. A central line was placed for management, and she was monitored for cardiac strain. Her condition improved over several days, with resolution of DKA, stabilization of kidney function, and improved mental status. She was transitioned to subcutaneous insulin and discharged with plans for outpatient follow-up in endocrinology and alcohol rehabilitation, along with prescriptions for naltrexone, pantoprazole, and all chronic medications.
